newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Pearson sees 20 mln stg currency hit.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Pearson sees 20 mln stg currency hit.

text.p: Full-year, pre-tax profits at Pearson Plc will be reduced by 20 million stg if the exchange rates at the end of June are maintained, Pearson finance director John Makinson said on Monday.
Makinson said currency factors at these rates would trim 120 million stg from sales, 22 million from operating profit and 20 million from pre-tax profit.

He said accounting problems at the company's Penguin USA unit had a "cash effect" of 48 million pounds in the first half of the year. But he said Pearson believed the 100 million stg provision taken last year to cover the losses should be "about right".
Makinson said Pearson was "actively reviewing" its diversified portfolio of businesses and that decisions had been made on the fate of some of them, but would not go into any further detail.
Pearson would have a "different looking portfolio" in less than five years, he said. Businesses were being evaluated in terms of scale and franchise value.
The company has set itself the goal of doubling in value over five years and achieving double digit earnings per share growth each year, Makinson confirmed. He described the targets as "stretching".

Pearson shares added 24p to 690p as the first-half results beat expectations. Analysts focused on the profits from continuing operations which almost doubled to 65.5 million stg, rather than the headline 81 million stg pre-tax figure.

Makinson highlighted what he termed a "very strong performance" from the Financial Times newspaper. The FT contributed operating profit of 22.4 million stg, up from 3.5 million a year ago, thanks to strong advertising revenues, a lower cost base and the absence of restructuring costs.
Penguin books has been boosted by the December acquisition of U.S. publisher Putnam Berkley, which Makinson said was being integrated very smoothly.

He noted that attributable profits from Pearson's investment banking associate Lazard were about 10 million stg below last year, meaning the improved profits were entirely down to the company's managed businesses.
